value.proposal_status: One supported reading retained; potential exceptions remain unresolved rather than formalized without evidence.

readings.subject: Mandatory e-IP routing for one IPD application or submission
readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] For one covered application or submission whose submission event falls on or after 30 November 2024, true means that the selected mandatory routing control is met because the event used e-IP; false means that the routing control is unmet. Outside this scope, no compliance determination is made. Unknown facts remain unknown. This is a proposed interpretation of the supplied text, not an approval or a determination of overall regulatory compliance.
readings.distinction: The phrase 'where practicable' qualifies the SFC's continuing review and enhancement of e-IP. It does not qualify the separate requirement that covered applications and submissions use e-IP. The parallel-run provision permits existing channels during a transitional period; it supplies no continuing exception after the stated cutover. Fee-payment functionality is permissive and does not itself expand the mandatory routing control to standalone fee payments.
readings.strongest_uncertainty: The referenced launch circular is unavailable. It may address transitional treatment, submission procedures or operational exceptions, but none can be established from this packet. The packet also does not determine the operative submission event for failed transmissions or filings spanning the cutover.
assumptions: The selected control concerns one actual application or submission, not overall regulatory compliance.
The submission event date governs the cutover. This is an interpretive assumption for continuing cases because the packet does not expressly address pending applications, amendments or resubmissions.
Extending the parallel run carries forward acceptance of existing channels through 29 November 2024. This inference is not needed to evaluate the selected post-cutover control.
A standalone annual-fee payment is not classified as a covered submission solely because e-IP supports payment.
No exception from unavailable material is assumed.

citations.quote: After the extended period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by the Investment Products Division (IPD)1 must be submitted to IPD via e-IP from 30 November 2024.
The SFC will continue to review and enhance the operation of e-IP where practicable.
During this period, the SFC continues to accept applications and submissions via existing channels.
To facilitate these enhancements, the SFC will extend the parallel run period of e-IP by one month to 29 November 2024.
In addition, e-IP users can also settle recurring annual fees associated with relevant investment products through the new system.

facts.name: is_covered_submission
facts.meaning: Whether the selected event is an application or submission to IPD concerning an investment product administered by IPD, interpreted with the listed product categories. Classification of borderline events requires judgment.

facts.name: submission_date
facts.meaning: Gregorian date of the selected submission event. Selecting the operative event for attempted, incomplete or continued filings may require judgment.

facts.name: submitted_via_e_ip
facts.meaning: Whether the selected application or submission was submitted to IPD through e-IP.

questions: Does the unavailable launch circular establish transitional treatment or an exception for any covered submission?
What event determines submission_date for an attempted, incomplete, amended or resubmitted filing?
Does an operational failure permit an alternative channel under material absent from this packet?

scope.interpretation: The obligation is attached to applications and submissions concerning investment products administered by IPD. Submitters are identified by their activity, not by an expressly named licence, institutional class or industry-wide status. The SFC is separately the actor extending the parallel run and reviewing the system.
scope.uncertainty: The packet does not comprehensively classify borderline events or identify every submitting actor.

definitions.interpretation: Footnote 1 supplies the named product categories for interpreting IPD scope. Footnote 2 expands WINGS. The juxtaposition of 'WINGS2' and footnote 2 supports reading the numeral as a footnote marker rather than evidence of a distinct portal.
definitions.uncertainty: The categories are not individually defined. Their application to a borderline product may require judgment. Typography is not independently available to verify the footnote-marker inference.

exceptions.interpretation: No express exception to the post-cutover routing requirement appears. 'Where practicable' attaches locally to the SFC's review and enhancement activity. Existing-channel acceptance is temporally confined to the parallel run. Optional fee payment concerns a separate function, not an exception for an otherwise covered submission.
exceptions.uncertainty: Exceptions in the unavailable dependency cannot be excluded or supplied.

modality.interpretation: 'Must' establishes the mandatory route within scope. 'Can also' permits annual-fee settlement through e-IP. Statements that the SFC 'will' extend, integrate, review or enhance describe announced administrative actions; they do not establish additional submitter obligations. The invitation to contact case officers is not a requirement to obtain approval or a waiver mechanism.
modality.uncertainty: Integration examples establish neither reporting triggers nor reporting deadlines.

time.interpretation: The source gives 29 July 2024 as launch, 29 October 2024 as the initial parallel-run endpoint, 29 November 2024 as its extended endpoint, and 30 November 2024 as the mandatory-routing start. The extension supersedes the initial endpoint. These are the historical dates stated in the packet.
time.uncertainty: Continued existing-channel acceptance in the extended month is inferred from the extension. Integration and fee-payment functionality have no independently specified effective dates. No present-day status beyond this packet is asserted.

dependencies.interpretation: The source expressly references the launch circular dated 8 July 2024. The packet identifies one unavailable dependency, provisionally associated with that circular. The supplied routing sentence supports a bounded proposal without importing missing provisions.
dependencies.uncertainty: The dependency identifier is not conclusively mapped to the named circular. Its definitions, procedures and exceptions remain uninspected; the proposal cannot establish complete treatment across related authority.

failed_hypotheses.substantive_effect: A covered post-cutover submission using another channel could meet the routing control if e-IP use were impracticable.
failed_hypotheses.assessment: Unsupported attachment. The qualification appears within the sentence about the SFC's continuing review and enhancement, with a different actor and action from the routing obligation.

failed_hypotheses.substantive_effect: Later submissions in existing cases would be exempt from e-IP routing.
failed_hypotheses.assessment: Unsupported. The acceptance provision concerns a period, not a cohort of cases. No supplied text grants grandfathering.

Starting 30 November 2024, ie, after the parallel run period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by IPD must be submitted via e-IP.

failed_hypotheses.assessment: Unsupported. The heading does not override the operative permissive wording.
